profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed to Prime, most likely Prime Data Centers given the California and Texas registry locations. Prime Data Centers own site states the company was established in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street, Dallas, Texas, under founder and CEO Nicholas Laag, and describes itself as majority founder owned. The company reports 28 data centers across 13 campuses globally with a 4 plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, and lists Silicon Valley and Dallas among its confirmed North America markets, alongside Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Sacramento, matching both states where this registry lists a Prime facility. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Prime Santa Clara publishes 57 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space at 26415 Corporate Ave in Santa Clara County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 57 MW of IT load is roughly 1,425 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 5,700 racks. Those two figures bracket the plausible range; which end applies depends on the workload mix, which the operator does not publish.

The three certifications define what the campus is qualified to host. SOC 2 Type 2 means the operator's controls over security, availability, and related trust criteria have been audited by an independent party over a sustained period. PCI DSS means the facility meets the payment card industry's physical and logical security requirements for handling cardholder data. ISO 27001 means an accredited body has certified the information security management system against that international standard. Together, the certifications qualify the campus for regulated and payment-sensitive workloads, but which tenants have chosen it is not published.

This site has mapped 103 data center facilities in California, of which 10 have published a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. Those 10 sum to 356 MW of published IT capacity. At 57 MW, Prime Santa Clara represents roughly 16 percent of that published total, and it ranks third among the facilities for which this site holds a comparable number. That rank reflects only what operators have chosen to publish, not the full installed base of the state.
